thread:
linda (Finance Manager): Heads-up: starting next Monday were enforcing a stricter PO-first policy for vendor invoices. Any vendor invoice over $1,000 must have a validated PO number before AP will approve payment. Please read the quick bullets and the Confluence page here: https://confluence.redwood.ai/finance/vendor-payments

sam (Eng Lead): Oof. Does this apply retroactively to invoices already in the pipeline?

linda (Finance Manager): No retroactive holds on invoices already approved in the system. For invoices received but not approved: AP will place a hold and request the PO. If you have a pending invoice, please open the procurement form and link the vendor ticket.

raj (Sourcing): Quick summary of changes:
- Invoices > $1,000 require PO prior to payment.
- Virtual card preferred for one-off vendor charges <$1,000.
- Recurring subscriptions need a subscription record and owner in the tracker.
- Foreign vendors: W-8 series required + local tax docs.
- AP SLA: 7 business days from receipt + PO.

accounts-payable-bot: Reminder: invoices without PO will be auto-tagged "waiting-for-PO" and receive an email to the requestor. Upload invoices to AP portal: https://pay.redwood.ai/invoices

sam (Eng Lead): For infra costs that fluctuate month-to-month (cloud overage bills), how should teams handle POs?

linda (Finance Manager): For variable monthly bills, create a standing PO for the estimated monthly spend with a "not-to-exceed" amount and attach the billing cadence. Update PO if actuals exceed the cap. If not feasible, use the virtual card and tag the project, but we prefer standing POs for predictable partners.

maria (People Ops): Do hiring/recruiting vendors count toward the $1k PO rule? Many recruiting invoices are >$1k.

raj (Sourcing): Recruiting invoices are included. Use the Talent Services category and create a PO or vendor contract before the agency bills. For urgent hires you can request an expedited PO (select "expedite" and justify in the procurement form).

sam (Eng Lead): Who signs POs? Manager vs procurement?

linda (Finance Manager): POs <$10k can be approved by the hiring/owning manager (via procurement form). POs >=$10k require procurement + finance sign-off.

accounts-payable-bot: New AP rule: payment runs are Tue/Thu. Approved invoices received by 11:59pm prior will be included in the next run.

sam (Eng Lead): Any changes to virtual card limits?

linda (Finance Manager): Default virtual card single-charge limit is $1,000. If you need higher for a specific vendor, request a temporary increase on the virtual card request form and include justification.

maria (People Ops): For contractors paid via invoice, do we still need W-9s?

raj (Sourcing): Yes for US contractors we need W-9. For non-US contractors we need the appropriate W-8 and local compliance docs. AP will reject invoices missing tax docs.

linda (Finance Manager): Quick checklist for requesters: 1) Submit procurement form for vendor/PO, 2) Create PO or request virtual card, 3) Attach SOW/invoice and tax docs, 4) Tag project owner and category. Missing items = hold.

sam (Eng Lead): Thanks. Can procurement add a short cheat-sheet for teams?

linda (Finance Manager): Yes  I uploaded a one-pager to Confluence under the vendor-payments page (section "cheat-sheet"). Also running a 15-min drop-in Q&A on Wednesday at 9am PT. Invite will be on the calendar.

accounts-payable-bot: If you need an exception, email payment-exceptions@redwood.ai with the ticket link and justification. Exceptions are triaged within 48 hours.

linda (Finance Manager): Last note: we'll run a soft audit in two weeks to surface missing POs and mis-tagged categories. If you get a ping from AP, please respond quickly to avoid late payment to vendors. Appreciate everyone being proactive on this. :handshake:
